description: Five protein mistakes quietly destroy muscle protein signals in skinny-fat guys who think they eat enough. Run the protein test, find which mistakes are yours, and rebuild the signal with the same food budget.

lines: The mistakes hide in the count.
beats.title: COUNT BEFORE YOU JUDGE

scenes.narration: Count it once more. | Yesterday's protein. | Meal by meal. | Honest grams. | Write the total. | And each meal's share. | Five mistakes hide | inside that count. | Most guys own three. | Some own all five. | Keep your numbers close. | At the end | I tell you | which mistakes are yours. | And what they cost.

beats.text: HITTING THE NUMBER IS NOT ENOUGH

scenes.label: THE TARGET THE MISTAKES STEAL FROM
scenes.narration: The target has not changed: about one point six grams of protein per kilo of bodyweight, one hundred and twelve grams for a seventy-kilo man. What this episode adds is the tax. Five common mistakes quietly tax that number, so a guy can hit one hundred and twelve on paper and deliver seventy to his muscles. A perfect total with a broken spread. Expensive protein burned as fuel because the rest of the diet is chaos. Liquid calories crowding the real food off the plate. Each mistake is small, deniable, and completely capable of holding a physique hostage for a year. By the end you will grade your own count against all five, and the verdict will not be comfortable, which is exactly why it will work.
scenes.sub: hit the number, lose it to mistakes - audit all five

lines: Muscle is built and lost daily.
beats.title: THE BALANCE SHEET

scenes.narration: Before the list, the accounting underneath it. Your muscle mass is not a statue, it is a balance sheet. Every day your body builds some muscle protein and breaks some down, and the difference, repeated for months, is your physique. Training and protein push the build side up. Chaos pushes the breakdown side up. The five mistakes in this episode all work the same quiet way: they shave the build side or feed the breakdown side, a few percent at a time, invisibly. No single mistake ruins anyone. That is what makes them dangerous. A ruined week gets noticed and fixed. A five-percent leak runs for a year, and the guy stands in the mirror wondering why nothing works when he does almost everything right. Almost is the address of these mistakes. We are going to walk through your count and find every leak, because on a light frame with a small surplus, five percent is not a detail. Five percent is the whole transformation, arriving or not arriving. And there is a sixth shadow mistake hovering over the five: treating protein as a weekend project or a payday purchase instead of a daily utility like electricity. Muscle does not experience your average intentions. It experiences today's deliveries, and it bills you daily in breakdown when they miss. The men who fix this stop thinking in terms of good weeks and bad weeks. They think in terms of an unbroken chain of ordinary days, each one delivering, because the chain is the physique.

beats.text: SKIP THE SOURCE, SKIP THE SIGNAL

scenes.narration: Mistake one: the dinner mountain. All your protein in one evening pile fires the synthesis trigger once, and the overflow cannot be banked for the morning. Mistake two: protein without an anchor source. Meals built on bread, rice and sauce carry five to ten grams of incidental protein and almost no leucine, so the trigger never fires even though the meal felt filling. These two mistakes are really one mistake, a scheduling mistake, and they are the most common pair in every skinny-fat food diary ever audited. The fix costs nothing: an anchor at every meal, eggs, dairy, meat, fish or legumes with grains, and the day's grams redistributed so each meal carries its own trigger. Look at your three meal numbers from the test. Any meal under fifteen grams is a leak with a name and an address, and now you know both. A practical word on sources while we are here. You do not need variety theater. Two or three anchors you genuinely like, rotated without ceremony, beat a rotating cast of exotic proteins you abandon by week two. Adherence is a nutrient. The best protein source in the world is the one still in your fridge in month four, being eaten at breakfast by a man who stopped having to think about it.

beats.text: JUICE AND SODA EAT YOUR PLATE

scenes.narration: Mistake three: eating so little overall that your protein gets burned as fuel. Amino acids are expensive bricks, but a starving body will burn bricks for heat, and a skinny-fat guy on an aggressive diet does exactly that: his hard-won protein becomes expensive firewood while his muscles get nothing. Maintenance calories are not a compromise, they are what lets protein do its one job. Mistake four: liquid crowding. Juice, soda and sweet coffee drinks fill the small stomach you actually have, and the chicken that was supposed to be lunch loses its seat. On a big appetite this is a rounding error. On yours it is the whole meal. Eat your protein as food, drink water like it is your job, and never let a beverage evict a building block from a stomach with limited seating.

lines: Five good days, two lost days:
the week still grades a C.
beats.title: THE WEEKLY AVERAGE

beats.text: GOOD ENOUGH DAILY BEATS PERFECT WEEKDAYS

scenes.narration: Mistake five is the politest and the deadliest: weekday perfection with weekend amnesia. Five days at one hundred and twenty grams and two days at fifty averages under one hundred, and muscle, which keeps daily books and does not respect your calendar stories, grades the week a C. The weekend body is the same body. It breaks down protein on Saturday exactly like Tuesday, and it would happily build on Saturday too if the bricks arrived. The fix is not weekend discipline, which fails by the second weekend. The fix is weekend-proof anchors: the yogurt that is always in the fridge, the eggs that take four minutes, the meal out ordered protein-first. Build a floor so low-effort days still deliver eighty percent, and your weekly average stops leaking the transformation you earned Monday to Friday.
Train with me. Four rounds, thirty seconds of split squats per side, twenty seconds of rest. Every order placed today gets delivered at your next meal. Go.

beats.text: FIXING ALL FIVE AT ONCE FAILS

scenes.narration: Fix them in order, one per week, because five simultaneous overhauls die together. Week one, the spread: move protein to breakfast until every meal has an anchor. Week two, the floor: set your weekend backup foods in place. Week three, the fuel: bring calories to maintenance and cut the liquid crowding. That is the whole repair, and it uses the food budget you already spend. The mistakes about the mistakes: buying supplements while meals still lack anchors, which is paying for delivery while the warehouse is empty. And auditing once, feeling informed, and never counting again, when the count is the only thing that keeps the leaks closed. Count one day a week, every week, like a man checking a bank balance he intends to grow.

beats.text: COUNT YOUR MISTAKES, NOT JUST GRAMS

scenes.label: THEN WE AUDIT THE FIVE AGAIN
scenes.narration: So, grade your count. Zero or one mistake: your protein signals are clean, and your remaining levers are load and sleep. Two or three: you are the classic case, a good total leaking a third of its value, and the three-week repair is your program. Four or five: do not feel attacked, feel located, because a full repair on a full leak is the fastest transformation in this entire season. Put your mistake count in the comments, zero to five, just the number. In thirty days we audit again, and a smaller number will mean your muscle protein signals finally receive what your grocery money already paid for.
scenes.sub: clean / leaking / full repair - the audit grades it

scenes.narration: Write your three fixes in order where you plan your food. Thirty days from now we audit the five mistakes again, and the count will tell us if the leaks are closed. If this helped, subscribe for the next test. This is {channel}. Train the cable.
